si_4_title.answer: Fractionating autism based on neuroanatomical normative modeling

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: The study uses the EU-AIMS Longitudinal European Autism Project (LEAP) cohort.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "We included 206 neurotypical (NT) ... and 316 participants with autism ... across 6 sites from the EU-AIMS LEAP sample"

answer.LEAP: normative training (NT subset); clinical application/clustering (ASD subset)

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: The normative model was trained on the Neurotypical (NT) cohort (N=206). The model was then applied to participants with autism (N=316) to estimate deviations (Normative Probability Maps) for clustering.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "GPR was trained on the NT cohort (N=206) ... We then created/calculated NPMs for participants with autism ... to partition the autism cohort into sub-clusters"

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: The model was trained on the full NT cohort of 206 participants using 10-fold cross-validation.
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: "We included 206 neurotypical (NT)... GPR was trained on the NT cohort (N=206)..."

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Age statistics for the NT cohort used for training. Min/Max inferred from the abstract's description of the full sample range.
dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.supporting_text: "We included 206 neurotypical (NT) (79 female, aged 17.5 ± 6.1 years)... aged 6 -31 years"

dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Calculated from Total N (206) and Female N (79). Male N = 206 - 79 = 127. Female % = 79/206. Male % = 127/206.
